For the term descending from Latin gamba (“leg”), compare typologically вступа́ть (vstupátʹ), выступа́ть (vystupátʹ) (akin to ступня́ (stupnjá)). For Latin gamba (“leg”) deriving from *kh₂em- (“to bend, to curve; …”), compare typologically кривоно́гий (krivonógij) (< криво́й (krivój) + нога́ (nogá)), кривору́кий (krivorúkij) (< криво́й (krivój) + рука́ (ruká)), als…

Borrowed from Finnish nieriä into Russian during the colonization of the Kamchatka (end of 17ᵗʰ, beginning of 18ᵗʰ century) by Finnish-Russian bilinguals, + -ка (-ka) ending. The meaning of the Finnish word is fixed to “saibling” now but it did not need to be so at that time. Doublet of нериас (nerias), нериус (nerius), and не́ргас (nérgas), northwestern Russian dialectal forms borrowed from Karelian nieries.
